changelog:
Record a programme — and the television answers back.

WHAT CHANGED

- Scheduled recording, proven on a phone. In Settings → Diagnostics (with Diagnostic mode on), "Record a two-minute test" records one of your live channels two minutes from now, for two minutes, into Movies/MobileIPTV as a .ts file any player opens. The phone wakes for it while asleep, shows a notice while recording (with Stop) and another when it finishes or fails, saying exactly what happened; anything still due is armed again after a restart. The first time, the phone asks you to allow "Alarms and reminders" for MobileIPTV.
- When a recording would start on a provider line already in use: the phone first looks for the same channel on another of your providers and records from there, leaving what is playing alone, and the finished notice says so ("Recorded from M as … (1.00: same guide id …)"). If there is no such channel and your paired television is using the line, the television asks you — "… is scheduled to record, but would interrupt this stream. Do you want to record or continue watching?" — and records only if you choose Record. If this phone's own stream is using the line, the phone's stream stops for the recording and tells you.
- "Ask the television a test question", beside the test recording in Diagnostics: sends the same question to your paired television so you can see the card and answer it; the phone shows what the television answered.
- A failed recording offers Retry now in its notice: same channel, same length, starting at once. A recording cut off because the phone was switched off or the app stopped is marked as such and its half-written file is removed. Recordings capture about twenty seconds before and after the programme. The "Recording…" notice goes away when the recording ends.

WHAT STAYS THE SAME

- Everything from 0.5.6: live transport controls, Continue watching, the refresh that changes only what changed, the licences page.

NOT YET

- Recording from the guide and a recordings list in the app: for now the Diagnostics row is the way to start one. Trimming the padding and compressing a finished recording.
